romeo-juliet.title: The First Kiss
romeo-juliet.setup: 凯普莱特家的舞会。罗密欧戴着面具混进仇家，第一眼看到朱丽叶就被迷住。他牵起她的手，两人用一首合写的十四行诗调情：他把自己比作朝圣者，把她比作圣徒。
romeo-juliet.acting: 这是一场游戏：两人都知道对方在调情，又都假装在谈宗教。罗密欧大胆，朱丽叶机智，每一句都在接住对方的球再抛回去。语速轻快，眼神不离开对方。

lines.en: If I profane with my unworthiest hand this holy shrine, the gentle fine is this:
lines.modern: If my unworthy hand has disrespected your holy hand, here is my gentle way to make up for it:
lines.zh: 如果我这卑微的手玷污了你这神圣的殿堂，我甘愿受这温柔的惩罚：
lines.note: profane 亵渎；shrine 圣殿（指朱丽叶的手）；fine 罚金

lines.en: My lips, two blushing pilgrims, ready stand to smooth that rough touch with a tender kiss.
lines.modern: My lips, like two shy pilgrims, are ready to fix that rough touch with a soft kiss.
lines.zh: 我的嘴唇，两个羞红脸的朝圣者，正准备用一个温柔的吻抚平那粗鲁的触碰。
lines.note: pilgrim 朝圣者。重读 lips 和 kiss

lines.en: Good pilgrim, you do wrong your hand too much, which mannerly devotion shows in this;
lines.modern: Good pilgrim, you are too hard on your hand. It only showed polite respect.
lines.zh: 好朝圣者，你太委屈你的手了，它这样做只是表达了恭敬的虔诚；
lines.note: do wrong 冤枉；devotion 虔诚

lines.en: For saints have hands that pilgrims' hands do touch, and palm to palm is holy palmers' kiss.
lines.modern: Saints have hands that pilgrims touch, and pressing palm to palm is a pilgrim's kiss.
lines.zh: 圣徒的手本就让朝圣者触碰，掌心贴着掌心，就是朝圣者的吻。
lines.note: palm 掌心 / palmer 朝圣者，双关。她在说：牵手就够了，不必亲

lines.en: Have not saints lips, and holy palmers too?
lines.modern: But don't saints and pilgrims have lips too?
lines.zh: 圣徒和朝圣者难道没有嘴唇吗？
lines.note: 句尾上扬，带一点坏笑

lines.en: Ay, pilgrim, lips that they must use in prayer.
lines.modern: Yes, pilgrim, lips they must use for praying.
lines.zh: 有的，朝圣者，那是用来祈祷的嘴唇。
lines.note: Ay = yes，读作 /aɪ/

lines.en: O, then, dear saint, let lips do what hands do; they pray, grant thou, lest faith turn to despair.
lines.modern: Then, dear saint, let our lips do what our hands do. They are praying: say yes, or my faith will turn into despair.
lines.zh: 那么，亲爱的圣徒，让嘴唇也像手一样吧；它们在祈祷，请你应允，免得信仰变成绝望。
lines.note: grant 应允；lest 以免

lines.en: Saints do not move, though grant for prayers' sake.
lines.modern: Saints don't move, even when they answer a prayer.
lines.zh: 圣徒不会主动，虽然会应允祈祷。
lines.note: 潜台词：我不会主动吻你，但也不会拒绝

lines.en: Then move not, while my prayer's effect I take. Thus from my lips, by yours, my sin is purged.
lines.modern: Then don't move, while I take what I prayed for. Now your lips have cleaned the sin from mine.
lines.zh: 那就别动，让我领受祈祷的回应。（吻她）这样，我唇上的罪借你的唇洗清了。
lines.note: purged 洗净。两句中间是吻，停一拍

lines.en: Then have my lips the sin that they have took.
lines.modern: Then my lips now have the sin they took from yours.
lines.zh: 那么你的罪就留在我的唇上了。
lines.note: 她在继续这个游戏，给他再吻一次的理由

lines.en: Sin from thy lips? O trespass sweetly urged! Give me my sin again.
lines.modern: Sin from my lips? What a sweet way to blame me! Give my sin back to me.
lines.zh: 罪从我的唇上过去了？多么甜蜜的责备！把我的罪还给我吧。
lines.note: thy = your。最后一句轻声，几乎是耳语

romeo-juliet.title: What's in a Name?
romeo-juliet.setup: 舞会后的深夜，朱丽叶独自站在阳台上，以为没人听见，说出她爱上了仇家的儿子。罗密欧正躲在下面的花园里。
romeo-juliet.acting: 朱丽叶不是在背诗，是在跟自己争论：她想找到一个能爱他的理由。wherefore 是“为什么”，不是“在哪里”，所以不要四处张望找罗密欧。她问的是：你为什么偏偏是罗密欧？

lines.en: O Romeo, Romeo! wherefore art thou Romeo?
lines.modern: Oh Romeo, Romeo! Why do you have to be Romeo?
lines.zh: 罗密欧啊，罗密欧！为什么你偏偏是罗密欧？
lines.note: wherefore = why（最常见的误解）；art thou = are you。重读 wherefore

lines.en: Deny thy father and refuse thy name; or, if thou wilt not, be but sworn my love, and I'll no longer be a Capulet.
lines.modern: Give up your father and your name. Or if you won't, just promise you love me, and I'll stop being a Capulet.
lines.zh: 否认你的父亲，抛弃你的姓氏吧；如果你不愿意，只要发誓爱我，我就不再姓凯普莱特。
lines.note: thou wilt = you will；sworn 发誓

lines.en: Shall I hear more, or shall I speak at this?
lines.modern: Should I keep listening, or should I say something now?
lines.zh: （旁白）我是继续听下去，还是现在就开口？
lines.note: 旁白：对观众说，声音小但要清楚

lines.en: 'Tis but thy name that is my enemy; thou art thyself, though not a Montague.
lines.modern: It's only your name that is my enemy. You would still be you, even if you weren't a Montague.
lines.zh: 只有你的姓氏是我的敌人；就算不姓蒙太古，你还是你。
lines.note: 'Tis = it is；but = only

lines.en: What's in a name? that which we call a rose by any other name would smell as sweet;
lines.modern: What does a name matter? A rose would smell just as sweet if we called it something else.
lines.zh: 名字有什么关系？我们叫作玫瑰的花，换个名字也一样芬芳；
lines.note: 全剧最有名的一句。rose 和 sweet 重读

lines.en: So Romeo would, were he not Romeo call'd, retain that dear perfection which he owes without that title.
lines.modern: In the same way, Romeo would still be perfect even if he weren't called Romeo.
lines.zh: 罗密欧也一样，就算不叫罗密欧，也依然保有他那可爱的完美。
lines.note: retain 保有；owes 在这里是 owns（拥有）

lines.en: Romeo, doff thy name, and for that name which is no part of thee take all myself.
lines.modern: Romeo, take off your name, and in exchange for it, which isn't really part of you, take all of me.
lines.zh: 罗密欧，抛掉你的名字吧，用这个本不属于你的名字，换走整个的我。
lines.note: doff 脱掉。take all myself 是全段的高潮，放慢

lines.en: I take thee at thy word: call me but love, and I'll be new baptized; henceforth I never will be Romeo.
lines.modern: I'll take you at your word! Just call me 'love', and I'll have a new name. From now on, I'll never be Romeo.
lines.zh: 我就照你的话：只要叫我“爱人”，我就重新受洗；从今以后，我再也不是罗密欧。
lines.note: 他突然现身，朱丽叶会被吓到。语气冲动、兴奋

lines.en: What man art thou that thus bescreen'd in night so stumblest on my counsel?
lines.modern: Who are you, hiding in the dark and listening to my secrets?
lines.zh: 你是谁？躲在黑夜里偷听我的心事？
lines.note: bescreen'd 遮蔽；counsel 心里话。受惊、警惕

lines.en: Art thou not Romeo and a Montague?
lines.modern: Aren't you Romeo, a Montague?
lines.zh: 你不是罗密欧，蒙太古家的人吗？
lines.note: 她认出了他的声音，害怕和惊喜同时出现

lines.en: Neither, fair saint, if either thee dislike.
lines.modern: Neither one, beautiful saint, if you don't like either.
lines.zh: 都不是，美丽的圣徒，如果你不喜欢其中任何一个。
lines.note: 他立刻用她刚才的话回答她

lines.en: If they do see thee, they will murder thee.
lines.modern: If they see you, they will kill you.
lines.zh: 他们要是看见你，会杀了你的。
lines.note: 整场最简单的一句，也是最真实的恐惧。不要演得太大

hamlet.title: To Be, or Not to Be
hamlet.setup: 哈姆雷特以为自己独自一人（其实国王和大臣正躲着偷看）。他在思考：活着忍受痛苦，和死去一了百了，哪一个更好？而死后的未知又让人不敢行动。
hamlet.acting: 这不是一段朗诵，而是一个人第一次把问题想清楚的过程。每个新想法都要“发现”出来，而不是早就知道。找到思考的节奏：提出问题、反驳自己、得出结论。

lines.en: To be, or not to be: that is the question:
lines.modern: To live, or to die: that is the question.
lines.zh: 生存还是毁灭，这是一个问题：
lines.note: 重读 be 和 not。不要一上来就悲伤，先是冷静地提出问题

lines.en: Whether 'tis nobler in the mind to suffer the slings and arrows of outrageous fortune,
lines.modern: Is it nobler to quietly suffer all the attacks that cruel luck throws at us,
lines.zh: 默默忍受命运暴虐的毒箭，
lines.note: slings 投石器；outrageous 残暴的。slings and arrows 连读

lines.en: Or to take arms against a sea of troubles, and by opposing end them?
lines.modern: or to fight back against an ocean of problems and end them by fighting?
lines.zh: 还是挺身反抗人世无涯的苦难，通过斗争把它们扫清？
lines.note: take arms 拿起武器。sea of troubles 是一个画面：问题像大海一样多

lines.en: To die: to sleep; no more;
lines.modern: To die is just to sleep, nothing more.
lines.zh: 死了，睡着了，什么都完了；
lines.note: 短句，中间停顿。像在试着说服自己

lines.en: and by a sleep to say we end the heart-ache and the thousand natural shocks that flesh is heir to,
lines.modern: and with that sleep we end the heartache and the thousand pains every human body is born with,
lines.zh: 要是在这一种睡眠之中，我们心头的创痛，以及其他无数血肉之躯所不能避免的打击，都可以从此消失，
lines.note: heir to 注定要继承的

lines.en: 'tis a consummation devoutly to be wish'd.
lines.modern: That is an ending we should truly wish for.
lines.zh: 那正是我们求之不得的结局。
lines.note: consummation 圆满的结局

lines.en: To die, to sleep; to sleep: perchance to dream: ay, there's the rub;
lines.modern: To die, to sleep. To sleep, maybe to dream. Ah, that's the problem.
lines.zh: 死了，睡着了；睡着了也许还会做梦；嗯，阻碍就在这里：
lines.note: perchance = maybe；rub 障碍。这里是“发现”的时刻，突然停住

lines.en: For in that sleep of death what dreams may come when we have shuffled off this mortal coil, must give us pause:
lines.modern: Because the dreams that might come in death, after we leave this life, make us stop and think.
lines.zh: 因为当我们摆脱了这具肉体之后，在那死亡的睡眠里，究竟会做些什么梦，那不能不使我们踌躇顾虑。
lines.note: shuffle off 摆脱；mortal coil 尘世的纷扰

lines.en: Thus conscience does make cowards of us all;
lines.modern: So thinking too much turns all of us into cowards.
lines.zh: 这样，重重的顾虑使我们全变成了懦夫；
lines.note: conscience 在这里是“思虑”。这是他的结论，也是对自己的批评

lines.en: And thus the native hue of resolution is sicklied o'er with the pale cast of thought,
lines.modern: and our natural courage gets weak and pale because we think too much,
lines.zh: 决心的赤热的光彩，被审慎的思维盖上了一层灰色，
lines.note: hue 颜色；resolution 决心。red 对 pale 的颜色对比

lines.en: And enterprises of great pith and moment with this regard their currents turn awry, and lose the name of action.
lines.modern: and great, important plans go off course and never become action.
lines.zh: 伟大的事业在这一种考虑之下，也会逆流而退，失去了行动的意义。
lines.note: pith and moment 分量与重要性。最后 action 一词说完，他看见了奥菲利娅

hamlet.title: I Did Love You Once
hamlet.setup: 奥菲利娅被父亲安排来退还哈姆雷特的情书和礼物，国王和她父亲就躲在旁边偷听。哈姆雷特察觉到了什么，开始对她忽冷忽热。
hamlet.acting: 两个人都在演戏：奥菲利娅在执行父亲的命令，哈姆雷特在装疯，又可能在试探她。真正的感情从裂缝里漏出来。“I did love you once”和“I loved you not”之间，要让观众分不清哪句是真的。

lines.en: Good my lord, how does your honour for this many a day?
lines.modern: My lord, how have you been these past days?
lines.zh: 殿下，您这些天来可好？
lines.note: 礼貌、小心翼翼。Good my lord 是敬称

lines.en: I humbly thank you; well, well, well.
lines.modern: Thank you very much. Fine, fine, fine.
lines.zh: 谢谢你，很好，很好，很好。
lines.note: 三个 well 每个都不一样：可以敷衍、讽刺或疲惫

lines.en: My lord, I have remembrances of yours, that I have longed long to re-deliver; I pray you, now receive them.
lines.modern: My lord, I have some gifts from you that I've wanted to give back for a long time. Please take them now.
lines.zh: 殿下，我有几件您送给我的纪念品，早就想还给您了；请您收下吧。
lines.note: remembrances 纪念品。她递出去的手在发抖

lines.en: No, not I; I never gave you aught.
lines.modern: No, not me. I never gave you anything.
lines.zh: 不，我没有，我从来没送过你什么东西。
lines.note: aught = anything。冷淡，拒绝接过

lines.en: My honour'd lord, you know right well you did;
lines.modern: My lord, you know very well you did.
lines.zh: 殿下，您明明知道您送过的；
lines.note: 受伤，但还在坚持

lines.en: For to the noble mind rich gifts wax poor when givers prove unkind. There, my lord.
lines.modern: To a noble person, a rich gift becomes worthless when the giver turns unkind. Here, my lord.
lines.zh: 对高尚的心灵来说，送礼的人变了心，再贵重的礼物也变得一文不值。拿去吧，殿下。
lines.note: wax = become。There 时把东西放下

lines.en: Ha, ha! are you honest?
lines.modern: Ha! Are you honest?
lines.zh: 哈哈！你贞洁吗？
lines.note: honest 在这里有“贞洁”的意思。突然的转变，让她措手不及

lines.en: My lord?
lines.modern: My lord?
lines.zh: 殿下？
lines.note: 困惑，害怕

lines.en: Are you fair?
lines.modern: Are you beautiful?
lines.zh: 你美丽吗？
lines.note: fair = beautiful

lines.en: What means your lordship?
lines.modern: What do you mean, my lord?
lines.zh: 殿下这是什么意思？

lines.en: I did love you once.
lines.modern: I did love you once.
lines.zh: 我曾经爱过你。
lines.note: 整场最安静的一句。did 重读，前面停一拍

lines.en: Indeed, my lord, you made me believe so.
lines.modern: Yes, my lord, you made me believe that.
lines.zh: 真的，殿下，您曾经让我相信是这样。
lines.note: 她终于说出真心话

lines.en: You should not have believed me; I loved you not.
lines.modern: You shouldn't have believed me. I didn't love you.
lines.zh: 你不该相信我的；我没有爱过你。
lines.note: 他在推开她。是残忍，还是在保护她？由你决定

macbeth.title: I Have Done the Deed
macbeth.setup: 深夜，麦克白刚刚刺杀了熟睡的国王邓肯。麦克白夫人在外面等他。两人在黑暗中低声说话，任何声音都让他们心惊。
macbeth.acting: 全场都是极短的句子，像心跳。两人几乎是耳语，但充满紧张。麦克白已经被吓坏了，麦克白夫人努力保持冷静。每一个声音（猫头鹰、蟋蟀）都让他们停下来听。

lines.en: I have done the deed. Didst thou not hear a noise?
lines.modern: I've done it. Didn't you hear a noise?
lines.zh: 我已经干了。你没有听见什么声音吗？
lines.note: deed 行为（指谋杀）；didst thou = did you。第一句压低声音，第二句突然警觉

lines.en: I heard the owl scream and the crickets cry. Did not you speak?
lines.modern: I heard an owl scream and crickets chirping. Didn't you say something?
lines.zh: 我听见猫头鹰在叫，蟋蟀在鸣。你没有说话吗？
lines.note: owl 猫头鹰（不祥之兆）；crickets 蟋蟀

lines.en: When?
lines.modern: When?
lines.zh: 什么时候？

lines.en: Now.
lines.modern: Just now.
lines.zh: 刚才。

lines.en: As I descended?
lines.modern: When I was coming down the stairs?
lines.zh: 在我下楼的时候？
lines.note: descend 下来。这四句要快，像乒乓球一样来回

lines.en: Ay.
lines.modern: Yes.
lines.zh: 是的。

lines.en: Hark! Who lies i' the second chamber?
lines.modern: Listen! Who is sleeping in the second bedroom?
lines.zh: 听！谁睡在第二间房里？
lines.note: Hark = listen；chamber 卧室

lines.en: Donalbain.
lines.modern: Donalbain.
lines.zh: 道纳本。
lines.note: 国王的小儿子

lines.en: This is a sorry sight.
lines.modern: This is a terrible sight.
lines.zh: （看着自己的手）这是一副悲惨的景象。
lines.note: sorry 在这里是“悲惨的”。他看着沾满血的双手

lines.en: A foolish thought, to say a sorry sight.
lines.modern: That's a foolish thing to say.
lines.zh: 说什么悲惨的景象，真是傻念头。
lines.note: 她用冷静和轻蔑来压住他的恐惧

lines.en: There's one did laugh in's sleep, and one cried 'Murder!' that they did wake each other: I stood and heard them:
lines.modern: One of them laughed in his sleep, and one cried 'Murder!', so they woke each other up. I stood there and listened.
lines.zh: 有一个人在睡梦里大笑，还有一个人喊“杀人啦！”，他们把彼此惊醒了；我站着听他们。
lines.note: in's = in his。他在重新经历刚才的恐怖

lines.en: One cried 'God bless us!' and 'Amen' the other; as they had seen me with these hangman's hands.
lines.modern: One said 'God bless us!' and the other said 'Amen', as if they had seen me with these killer's hands.
lines.zh: 一个喊“上帝保佑我们！”，另一个说“阿门”，好像他们看见了我这双刽子手的手。
lines.note: hangman 刽子手。说到 hands 时看着手

macbeth.title: Tomorrow, and Tomorrow
macbeth.setup: 敌军包围了城堡。仆人报告：王后死了。麦克白已经失去了一切，连悲伤都感觉不到。他说出了莎士比亚笔下最绝望的一段话，把人生比作一个拙劣的演员。
macbeth.acting: 不要演“悲痛”。麦克白的问题是他已经什么都感觉不到了。声音平静、空洞、疲惫，到 poor player 和 stage 时，作为演员的你会感受到这句话的分量。

lines.en: She should have died hereafter; there would have been a time for such a word.
lines.modern: She would have died sooner or later. There would have been a time for that news.
lines.zh: 她反正要死的，迟早总会有听到这个消息的一天。
lines.note: hereafter 以后。语气疲惫，几乎没有反应

lines.en: To-morrow, and to-morrow, and to-morrow, creeps in this petty pace from day to day
lines.modern: Tomorrow, and tomorrow, and tomorrow, crawls slowly along, day after day,
lines.zh: 明天，明天，再一个明天，一天接着一天地蹑步前进，
lines.note: 三个 tomorrow 越来越慢，越来越沉。creep 爬行；petty 琐碎的

lines.en: To the last syllable of recorded time,
lines.modern: until the very last moment of time.
lines.zh: 直到最后一秒钟的时间；
lines.note: syllable 音节

lines.en: And all our yesterdays have lighted fools the way to dusty death.
lines.modern: And all our past days have only lit the way for fools to die and turn to dust.
lines.zh: 我们所有的昨天，不过替傻子们照亮了到死亡的土壤中去的路。
lines.note: dusty death：人死后归于尘土

lines.en: Out, out, brief candle!
lines.modern: Go out, go out, short little candle!
lines.zh: 熄灭了吧，熄灭了吧，短促的烛光！
lines.note: 整段唯一的爆发。candle 是生命

lines.en: Life's but a walking shadow, a poor player that struts and frets his hour upon the stage
lines.modern: Life is just a walking shadow, a bad actor who shows off and worries during his hour on stage,
lines.zh: 人生不过是一个行走的影子，一个在舞台上指手画脚的拙劣演员，
lines.note: player = actor；strut 昂首阔步；fret 焦躁。对演员来说最刺痛的一句

lines.en: And then is heard no more: it is a tale told by an idiot,
lines.modern: and then is never heard from again. It is a story told by an idiot,
lines.zh: 登场片刻，就在无声无息中悄然退下；它是一个愚人所讲的故事，
lines.note: heard no more 声音渐弱

lines.en: Full of sound and fury, signifying nothing.
lines.modern: full of noise and anger, but meaning nothing.
lines.zh: 充满着喧哗和骚动，却找不到一点意义。
lines.note: fury 狂怒；signify 意味着。nothing 说完，留一段长长的沉默

midsummer.title: Bottom Wants Every Part
midsummer.titleZh: 选角会·波顿什么都想演
midsummer.setup: 一群雅典工匠要为公爵的婚礼排一出戏。导演昆斯在分配角色，织布工波顿是个自信爆棚的业余演员，什么角色都想演。这是莎士比亚写的“剧组选角现场”。
midsummer.acting: 喜剧的关键是角色自己完全认真。昆斯努力维持秩序，波顿真心觉得自己是天才。波顿的“暴君台词”要演得夸张、用力过猛，那正是笑点。

lines.en: Is all our company here?
lines.modern: Is everyone in our group here?
lines.zh: 咱们的人都到齐了吗？
lines.note: company 剧团。像导演开会第一句

lines.en: You were best to call them generally, man by man, according to the scrip.
lines.modern: You'd better call them one by one, according to the list.
lines.zh: 你最好照着名单，一个一个地点名。
lines.note: 波顿用错了词：generally 应该是 individually，他总是爱用大词又用错

lines.en: Here is the scroll of every man's name, which is thought fit, through all Athens, to play in our interlude before the duke and the duchess, on his wedding-day at night.
lines.modern: Here's the list of everyone in Athens who is good enough to act in our play for the duke and duchess on their wedding night.
lines.zh: 这儿是全雅典公认最适合在公爵和公爵夫人结婚那天晚上，在他们面前演出的人员名单。
lines.note: interlude 短剧。昆斯很骄傲

lines.en: First, good Peter Quince, say what the play treats on, then read the names of the actors, and so grow to a point.
lines.modern: First, Peter Quince, tell us what the play is about, then read the actors' names, and get to the point.
lines.zh: 彼得·昆斯，先说说这出戏讲的是什么，然后念演员的名字，然后言归正传。
lines.note: 他一直在指挥导演

lines.en: Marry, our play is, The most lamentable comedy, and most cruel death of Pyramus and Thisby.
lines.modern: Well, our play is called 'The Very Sad Comedy and Very Cruel Death of Pyramus and Thisby'.
lines.zh: 好，咱们的戏名是：《最可悲的喜剧，以及皮拉摩斯和提斯柏的最残酷的死》。
lines.note: lamentable comedy“可悲的喜剧”本身就是个笑话。Marry 是口头语，相当于 Well

lines.en: A very good piece of work, I assure you, and a merry.
lines.modern: A very good play, I promise you, and a fun one.
lines.zh: 一出很好的戏，我向你保证，而且很有趣。
lines.note: 他其实还没读过

lines.en: Answer as I call you. Nick Bottom, the weaver.
lines.modern: Answer when I call your name. Nick Bottom, the weaver.
lines.zh: 我叫到谁，谁就答应。织工尼克·波顿。

lines.en: Ready. Name what part I am for, and proceed.
lines.modern: Ready! Tell me my part, and keep going.
lines.zh: 有！说我演什么角色，然后接着念。
lines.note: 立刻站起来，非常积极

lines.en: You, Nick Bottom, are set down for Pyramus.
lines.modern: Nick Bottom, you are playing Pyramus.
lines.zh: 你，尼克·波顿，派定演皮拉摩斯。

lines.en: What is Pyramus? a lover, or a tyrant?
lines.modern: Who is Pyramus? A lover, or a tyrant?
lines.zh: 皮拉摩斯是什么人？一个情人，还是一个暴君？
lines.note: tyrant 暴君。演员拿到角色的第一个问题

lines.en: A lover, that kills himself most gallant for love.
lines.modern: A lover who kills himself very bravely for love.
lines.zh: 一个情人，为了爱情最英勇地自杀了。
lines.note: gallant 英勇地

lines.en: That will ask some tears in the true performing of it: if I do it, let the audience look to their eyes; I will move storms.
lines.modern: That will need some real tears. If I play it, the audience had better watch out for their eyes. I will make them cry like a storm.
lines.zh: 要演得逼真，那可得掉几滴眼泪：要是我来演，观众们可得当心他们的眼睛，我要让他们哭成一片暴风雨。
lines.note: 他已经在想象自己的成功了。越说越大声

midsummer.title: If We Shadows Have Offended
midsummer.setup: 全剧结束，小精灵迫克独自走到台前对观众说话：如果这出戏让你们不满意，就当是做了一场梦吧。请鼓掌，我们会做得更好。
midsummer.acting: 打破第四面墙，直接看着观众说话。语气调皮又真诚，像在跟观众商量。押韵很重要：offended/mended，here/appear，读出节奏感。最后一句是请观众鼓掌。

lines.en: If we shadows have offended, think but this, and all is mended,
lines.modern: If we actors have upset you, just think this, and everything will be fine:
lines.zh: 要是我们这些影子惹您不快，只要这样想，一切就都好了：
lines.note: shadows 影子，也指演员。offended 冒犯 / mended 修补，押韵

lines.en: That you have but slumber'd here while these visions did appear.
lines.modern: that you were only sleeping here while you saw these dreams.
lines.zh: 您只是在这里睡了一觉，看见了这些幻象。
lines.note: slumber 睡觉；vision 幻象

lines.en: And this weak and idle theme, no more yielding but a dream,
lines.modern: And this silly little story is nothing more than a dream,
lines.zh: 这个无聊又荒唐的故事，不过是一场梦而已，
lines.note: idle 无聊的

lines.en: Gentles, do not reprehend: if you pardon, we will mend:
lines.modern: Ladies and gentlemen, don't blame us. If you forgive us, we will do better.
lines.zh: 诸位，请别责怪；您若原谅，我们会改进。
lines.note: Gentles = 各位观众；reprehend 责备；pardon 原谅

lines.en: And, as I am an honest Puck, if we have unearned luck now to 'scape the serpent's tongue,
lines.modern: And, as I'm an honest Puck, if we're lucky enough to escape your hissing,
lines.zh: 我迫克说话算数，要是我们侥幸没有被嘘下台，
lines.note: serpent's tongue 蛇的嘶嘶声 = 观众的嘘声

lines.en: We will make amends ere long; else the Puck a liar call;
lines.modern: we'll make it up to you soon. If not, you can call Puck a liar.
lines.zh: 我们很快就会补偿各位；否则就叫我迫克是个骗子。
lines.note: amends 补偿；ere long 不久

lines.en: So, good night unto you all.
lines.modern: So, good night to all of you.
lines.zh: 那么，祝大家晚安。
lines.note: 鞠躬的位置

lines.en: Give me your hands, if we be friends, and Robin shall restore amends.
lines.modern: Give me your applause if we're friends, and Robin will make everything right.
lines.zh: 如果我们是朋友，就请鼓鼓掌吧，罗宾一定会报答各位。
lines.note: Give me your hands = 请鼓掌。Robin 是迫克的另一个名字

seagull.title: Why Do You Always Wear Black?
seagull.setup: 夏日傍晚，湖边庄园。穷教师梅德维坚科暗恋管家的女儿玛莎，每天走六英里来看她。玛莎却总是一身黑衣，冷淡地回应他。这是现代戏剧最有名的开场之一。
seagull.acting: 契诃夫的台词表面是闲聊，底下全是没说出口的感情（潜台词）。梅德维坚科在求爱，玛莎在拒绝，但两人都没直说。台词要像日常说话，不要“念”。

lines.en: Why do you always wear mourning?
lines.modern: Why do you always wear black?
lines.zh: 你为什么总是穿黑衣服？
lines.note: mourning 丧服。开场第一句，好奇中带着关心

lines.en: I dress in black to match my life. I am unhappy.
lines.modern: I wear black to match my life. I'm unhappy.
lines.zh: 我在为我的生活服丧。我不幸福。
lines.note: 整部戏的基调。说得平淡，不要哭

lines.en: Why should you be unhappy? I don't understand it.
lines.modern: Why would you be unhappy? I don't get it.
lines.zh: 你为什么会不幸福？我不明白。
lines.note: 他真的不懂

lines.en: You are healthy, and though your father is not rich, he has a good competency.
lines.modern: You're healthy, and your father isn't rich, but he has enough money.
lines.zh: 你身体健康，你父亲虽然不富有，但也过得去。
lines.note: competency 足够的收入

lines.en: My life is far harder than yours. I only have twenty-three roubles a month to live on, but I don't wear mourning.
lines.modern: My life is much harder than yours. I only have twenty-three roubles a month, but I don't wear black.
lines.zh: 我的日子比你难过得多。我一个月只有二十三卢布，可我也没穿丧服。
lines.note: rouble 卢布。他总是在说钱

lines.en: Happiness does not depend on riches; poor men are often happy.
lines.modern: Happiness doesn't depend on money. Poor people are often happy.
lines.zh: 幸福不在于有钱；穷人也常常很幸福。
lines.note: riches 财富

lines.en: In theory, yes, but not in reality.
lines.modern: In theory, yes, but not in real life.
lines.zh: 理论上是这样，现实中可不是。

lines.en: The play will soon begin.
lines.modern: The play is about to start.
lines.zh: （望向舞台）戏快开演了。
lines.note: 她在转移话题

lines.en: There is no ground on which your soul and mine can meet. I love you.
lines.modern: Our souls have nothing in common. I love you.
lines.zh: 你的灵魂和我的灵魂没有共同之处。我爱你。
lines.note: 终于说出口了。I love you 简单、直接

lines.en: It is not that. I am touched by your affection, but I cannot return it, that is all.
lines.modern: It's not that. Your love touches me, but I can't love you back, that's all.
lines.zh: 不是因为这个。你的感情让我感动，但我无法回报，就是这样。
lines.note: affection 爱慕；return 回报。温和地拒绝

lines.en: Will you take some?
lines.modern: Would you like some?
lines.zh: （递过鼻烟盒）你要来一点吗？
lines.note: 拒绝之后立刻递鼻烟，典型的契诃夫式尴尬

lines.en: No, thank you.
lines.modern: No, thank you.
lines.zh: 不了，谢谢。
lines.note: 之后是一段停顿。停顿也是表演

seagull.title: I Am an Actress
seagull.setup: 两年后的风雨夜，妮娜突然回到庄园见特里波列夫。她当年离家去当演员，经历了失恋、失去孩子、演得一塌糊涂。现在她终于明白了做演员真正重要的是什么。
seagull.acting: 这是写给所有演员的一段独白。妮娜疲惫、精神恍惚，常常说到一半忘了自己在说什么（“I am a sea-gull — no”）。但最后她找到了力量。从破碎走向坚定，是这段戏的弧线。

lines.en: I am so tired. If I could only rest—rest.
lines.modern: I'm so tired. If only I could rest, just rest.
lines.zh: 我太累了。要是能休息一下该多好，休息一下。
lines.note: 趴在桌上。第二个 rest 更轻

lines.en: I am a sea-gull—no—no, I am an actress.
lines.modern: I'm a seagull. No, no, I'm an actress.
lines.zh: 我是一只海鸥……不，不，我是一个演员。
lines.note: 她在海鸥（被毁掉的人）和演员（她的身份）之间挣扎

lines.en: He does not believe in the theatre; he used to laugh at my dreams,
lines.modern: He doesn't believe in the theatre. He used to laugh at my dreams,
lines.zh: 他不相信戏剧；他总是嘲笑我的梦想，
lines.note: 他 = 特里果林，她爱过的作家

lines.en: so that little by little I became down-hearted and ceased to believe in it too.
lines.modern: so slowly I lost hope and stopped believing in it too.
lines.zh: 于是我渐渐地灰了心，自己也不再相信了。
lines.note: down-hearted 灰心；cease 停止

lines.en: I never knew what to do with my hands, and I could not walk properly or control my voice.
lines.modern: I never knew what to do with my hands, and I couldn't walk right or control my voice.
lines.zh: 我不知道手该往哪儿放，不会在台上走路，也控制不了自己的声音。
lines.note: 每个演员都经历过的噩梦

lines.en: You cannot imagine the state of mind of one who knows as he goes through a play how terribly badly he is acting.
lines.modern: You can't imagine how it feels to know, in the middle of a play, how terribly you are acting.
lines.zh: 你想象不到，一个人在演戏时清楚地知道自己演得有多糟，那是什么滋味。

lines.en: I have changed now. Now I am a real actress.
lines.modern: I've changed now. Now I'm a real actress.
lines.zh: 现在我变了。现在我是一个真正的演员了。
lines.note: 转折点。抬起头，声音变得坚定

lines.en: I act with joy, with exaltation, I am intoxicated by it, and feel that I am superb.
lines.modern: I act with joy and excitement. I'm drunk on it, and I feel wonderful.
lines.zh: 我演戏时满心欢喜，兴奋不已，我陶醉其中，觉得自己好极了。
lines.note: exaltation 狂喜；intoxicated 陶醉；superb 极好

lines.en: For us, whether we write or act, it is not the honour and glory of which I have dreamt that is important, it is the strength to endure.
lines.modern: For people like us, writers or actors, what matters isn't the fame I dreamed about. It's the strength to keep going.
lines.zh: 对我们来说，不管是写作还是演戏，重要的不是我梦想过的荣誉和名声，而是忍耐的力量。
lines.note: 整部戏的核心。endure 忍耐、坚持。慢下来，每个词都要清楚

lines.en: One must know how to bear one's cross, and one must have faith.
lines.modern: You have to know how to carry your burden, and you have to believe.
lines.zh: 一个人要懂得背起自己的十字架，要有信念。
lines.note: bear one's cross 承受苦难

lines.en: I believe, and so do not suffer so much, and when I think of my calling I do not fear life.
lines.modern: I believe, so I don't suffer as much. And when I think about my calling, I'm not afraid of life.
lines.zh: 我有信念，所以不那么痛苦了；一想到我的使命，我就不再害怕生活。
lines.note: calling 使命、天职。最后一句给自己，也给所有想当演员的人

lines.en: You have found your way, you know where you are going, but I am still groping in a chaos of phantoms and dreams.
lines.modern: You've found your path. You know where you're going. But I'm still lost in a mess of ghosts and dreams.
lines.zh: 你找到了自己的路，你知道该往哪里去；可我还在幻影和梦想的混沌中摸索。
lines.note: grope 摸索；chaos 混乱。悲伤，他被留在了原地
